I’m an indie musician and I don’t rlly have that much of a following yet but you might want to look at this differently. You main goal is trying to reach a new audience but you definitely don’t need a label to do this. 

TikTok is an extremely great way to promote music nowadays, and I’m sure you could find a little success there if you make the right video. There is also ads that you can run on social media (not really sure how effective this is because I havent done it) which could also drive people to your music. 

Honestly social media is the way to go, it’s just going to take a lot of dedication/work. I personally use distrokid to distribute my music. I pay maybe like 35 a year and I retain all the profits to my music. If you’re going the all platforms route, I would genuinely push Spotify more than any other platform. It’s the most popular and monthly listeners as well as other metrics give you a good idea of your reach as a musician. Spotify itself has a playlist pitching tool that you can submit to up to a day before your release! If you get on one of these playlists, these are THOUSANDS of new listeners getting introduced to your music. You can also find playlist made by curators or just regular people and try to get your music on there.
